title: Issue status does not establish fix coverage or novelty
applies_when: A source-audit lead resembles an open or closed issue, a merged fix to a sibling method, a multi-case report, or a prior no-op restriction whose return-value contract was not checked.
lesson: Read the issue body, latest discussion and linked patch before deciding whether a finding is new or fixed. An open issue can already have a reporter-confirmed repair: Megatron #8179's comments point to #7582 and report that the original tied-weight reproducer passed. Preserve author ownership, not a competing fix based only on the initial body. Separate three questions: is the behavior reproducible now, was this exact case already reported, and did the accepted patch address it? AnyIO #1081 also reports negative receive_exactly, beyond the receive API in its title; merged #1191's max_bytes validation does not prove exact-read coverage. Return to that report rather than claiming fresh discovery. Similarly, a maintainer's prohibition on moving a stream position does not require an accepted no-op seek to return None: check the actual return contract and consumer separately. An existing repair or passing characterization test is not evidence that every remaining behavior was deliberately requested. Record scoped advice without suppressing the whole file or rewriting raw model answers.
avoid_when: Reporter-confirmed repair is not our independent native qualification, proof of merge or all-case support. A current native failure does not prove novelty, intended behavior or maintainer acceptance. Do not copy a sibling API's positive-size constraint: zero-length exact reads can differ from bounded receive. Preserve streaming restrictions when repairing no-op returns; a synchronous BufferedReader reproduction does not prove async zip/tar compatibility or justify random access. These are scoped counterexamples, not a measured Scout conversion/miss-rate improvement or a universal rule to reopen closed issues.

evidence.note: The closed report explicitly includes negative and zero receive_exactly cases and reproducer tests, beyond the receive(max_bytes) API named in its title. It establishes prior reporting, not the final contract for every case.
The merged follow-on describes validation of max_bytes in ByteReceiveStream.receive implementations. Its closure of #1081 alone does not establish receive_exactly coverage.

Pinned source still uses buffer[:nbytes] when remaining <= 0, with no negative-nbytes guard. This is scoped current-source evidence, not proof that the behavior is supported, novel or accepted for repair.
The maintainer asks that async/streaming files not be seekable. This addresses position-changing seeks, not an explicit requirement that permitted no-op calls return None.
After merged #2214, both HTTP stream classes still return None from accepted no-op seeks. Same-function repair history does not remove this distinct return-value behavior.

Proposed follow-up returns current offsets without enabling random access. Exact-source loopback BufferedReader raises TypeError before and returns integer positions after; 110 official HTTP cases pass. Open PR, not maintainer acceptance, full CI or measured selector utility.

The open issue's Oct14 discussion points to PR7582; the reporter confirms the original tied-weight reproduction completes two iterations, validation and test. This is reported evidence, not our execution or a merge verdict.

An existing author-owned repair already addresses OneToOne.update dropping the first pair of one-shot iterables. Independent Linux CPython3.12 checking of exact head e5f2c7b gives 50 focused passes; unchanged 4e5faa3 with identical author tests gives 43 passes and 7 failures, with all other outcomes unchanged. No competing repair is needed. This is focused native evidence, not installed tox, the complete interpreter/OS matrix or maintainer acceptance.

The prior open PR already reports CachedFunction ignoring scoped=True and provides its own reproduction/repair. The PR body and committed change description match that hypothesis; this entry does not independently qualify its head. Current main can retain a real bug while a matching repair waits upstream. Check current discussions before spending another discovery batch; a stale search-engine snapshot or an empty collected item list is not evidence of novelty.

Pinned OneToOne.update still consumes a pair before materializing the remaining iterator, despite the already-open PR523. Reproduction and novelty are separate questions. Do not suppress the whole module: copy, serialization or other update subcases need their own contract, duplicate and native checks.

Pinned CachedFunction still omits scoped from key construction while PR498 already exists. Source affinity makes this prior report available to the next audit, not an automatic negative label, universal file exclusion or measured improvement in discovery yield.
